claims.text: TOR-TILD conventionally uses EAM potentials as references for free-energy calculations.
Conventional EAM references exhibit a large thermodynamic-integration path mismatch for high-temperature multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The EAM path mismatch results from limited representation of high-temperature atomic configurations.
The proposed intervention is to train and implement an MLIP on a diverse set of high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations.
The enriched MLIP training set captures a wide diversity of atomic configurations present in the ab initio liquid.
Training on many high-temperature configurations enables the MLIP to reproduce the ab initio free-energy landscape more accurately than a standard EAM reference.
More accurate reproduction of the free-energy landscape improves phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The MLIP will significantly reduce TI path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's standard EAM references.
The TI path mismatch may decrease by approximately 50% relative to the EAM-reference result.
Analogous elemental and binary calculations have demonstrated the predicted reduction in TI path mismatch.
The intervention applies to multicomponent alloys with multiple principal elements in both solid and liquid phases around and slightly above their melting points.
The expected improvement is primarily confined to multicomponent HEAs near their melting temperatures.
Performance may vary outside the near-melting temperature range or for alloys with extreme compositional complexity.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on training-data quality and potential architecture.
Mismatch reduction will vary among HEA compositions.
